catalog_quote: There are two prosodic phenomena whose description demands a sentence be segmented into a series of phonological phrases. One of these phenomena is accent (characterized by high pitch). Chimwiini has an accentual contrast between penultimate (second syllable from end) and ultimate (final syllable). This accentual contrast is dependent mostly on morphosyntactic considerations, but what is crucial for the concerns of the present paper is that it is a phrasal rather than a word-level phenomenon. ... At the (prosodic) word level, each word bears an accent. In the default case, accent is on the penult (if there is a penult, otherwise on the only syllable). Under specific morphosyntactic conditions, accent is final. The accented syllable may also be referred to as the H-toned syllable, since its only consistent phonetic marking is a pitch level that is higher than the preceding syllable ... A…

(2) Deciding source: a 2010 open-access phonology article by Kisseberth, who with Abasheikh is the sole primary describer of Chimwiini prosody since 1974; Glottolog has no grammar or phonology entries for chim1312 and web search finds no competing description or instrumental study by anyone else. sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles W. 2011. Phonological phrasing and questions in Chimwiini. ZAS Papers in Linguistics 55: 83-116. doi:10.21248/zaspil.55.2011.410
sources.quote: 'Each phonological phrase bears a single accent (realized as High tone). This accent always resides on the final prosodic word in the phrase. In certain morphosyntactic environments, this accent is on the final syllable of the word. In the default case, it is on the penult syllable.' Final-accent triggers listed: 1st/2nd person subject present/past, relative clauses, conditional ka tense, conjunction na 'and', certain lexical items. Refines our exceptions list (record names only two triggers) but not the classification.

sources.citation: Henderson, Brent. 2010. Chimwiini: endangered status and syntactic distinctiveness. Journal of West African Languages 37(1): 75-91.
sources.quote: 'while accent typically falls on the penultimate syllable of phrases in Chimwiini, in first and second person (both singular and plural) verb phrases, it falls on the final syllable'; fn.13 'Accent is on the penultimate syllable of each phrases unless otherwise marked'. Independent author (syntactician, own fieldwork with diaspora speakers) adopting the same phrasal-accent description, citing K&A.

sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles W. & Mohammad Imam Abasheikh. 2009 ms. Chimwiini Phonological Phrasing Revisited (pre-publication version of Lingua 121(13):1987-2013, 2011; PDF dated 22 Jul 2009, EGG 2009 course materials).
sources.quote: 'The accented syllable in Chimwiini has an entirely consistent phonetic attribute: it is characterized by high pitch. ... accent falls either on the penult syllable or the final syllable of a word ... The default accent is penult. Final accent occurs only in certain morphological or syntactic structures' (3.0); 'all the words in a sentence are organized into phrases, and each phrase has one and only one accented word and that word is the last one in the phrase' (3.8); 'it is correct to say that accent in Chimwiini is a phrasal phenomenon rather than a word-levl phenomenon' (3.9).
